newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ROW FUELS INTENSE LIVERPOOL-UNITED RIVALRY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ROW FUELS INTENSE LIVERPOOL-UNITED RIVALRY.

text.p: A heated public row between Manchester United boss Alex Ferguson and Liverpool's Roy Evans will guarantee an even fiercer rivalry than usual when their teams meet on Saturday in a possible English championship decider at Anfield.

Ferguson is reported to be furious with Evans -- and with Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger -- for their opposition to the idea that United should be allowed more time to complete their over-crowded fixture list.

Historically it has never taken much to set United and Liverpool against each other. While Liverpool have an intense rivalry with their near neighbours Everton, it has none of the elements of venomous loathing that the red-shirted fans of Liverpool reserve for the red-shirted battalions of United.
This latest squabble does nothing to calm their rivalry and neither club has been slow to criticise the other in public.
Evans made his feelings public last week when he said: "If Manchester United were to be given an extra week to complete their fixtures it would be totally out of order.
"No club should gain an advantage. Like them, we have to play four games inside nine days and it seems like a funny time to start changing the rules."

Ferguson, fuelling the confrontation that his club started, said he believed that Liverpool and Arsenal, the only other clubs still in the hunt for the title, had conspired to force the premier league to refuse United the extra time they had asked for.

United chairman Martin Edwards accused the league of being "amateurish" when they refused United an extension and called their decision ludicrous. United are considering whether to appeal against the ruling in the courts.
The entire row -- which has repercussions for clubs at the bottom of the premier league and in other divisions -- has done nothing to ease the tension before Saturday's match.

Liverpool's rivalry with United -- then known as Newton Heath -- began on April 28 1894 when Liverpool won a "test match", an early version of the modern play-off, 2-0 and were promoted into the first division at the expense of the Manchester team.

Their first league meeting proper came two years later when Liverpool won 7-1 and the impact of those shattering defeats by their Lancashire foes helped to set in motion a feud which has lasted without much let-up ever since.
Geographically the cities are close and the two teams mirror each other in terms of their self-image and achievements.

The modern-day Liverpool was built on the foundations laid by a Scot -- Bill Shankly. The modern United owe their existence to Shankly's Scottish friend and rival Sir Matt Busby who rebuilt the club after Old Trafford was badly damaged by bombs in the Second World War.

Manchester United have won the European Cup and so have Liverpool -- four times to United's once. Liverpool have won a record 18 league titles, United have won 10. United have won the F.A. Cup a record nine times, Liverpool five. Liverpool have won the double once, United are the only club to have won it twice.

United prevented Liverpool winning the double in 1977 when they beat them in the Cup Final at Wembley but Liverpool could not stop United winning it last year when United beat them in the Cup Final again.

While United have had the better of their meetings in the Cup down the years, their league record is almost identical. Of the 127 matches played, each side have won 44 with 39 drawn. United have scored 134 goals, Liverpool 133.
While Liverpool dominated the English league and won 11 championships between 1973 and 1990, United had to be content with nothing better than two runners-up spots in 1980 and 1988.
But since 1993 matters have been very different with United winning three titles in the last four seasons and Liverpool finishing no higher than third.
It is not only the fans who are rooted in either one camp or the other -- few players have ever made the short move directly between the two clubs.
The last to do so was Phil Chisnall a 21-year-old winger who went from United to Liverpool for 25,000 pounds, 33 years ago this month.
Only three other players have ever moved directly from Old Trafford to Anfield and only five players have gone in the other direction and the last of those was nearly 60 years ago.

He was Allenby Chilton who was a member of United's 1948 F.A. Cup winning team and helped them to win the title in 1952. He joined United in 1938 and made his debut for them on September 2 1939, the day before England went to war with Germany.

United go to Liverpool as league leaders with 66 points from 33 matches. Arsenal are second on 63 points and Liverpool third on the same number but Liverpool can go clear at the top if they win at Everton in the Merseyside derby on Wednesday and beat United.
